meaning: The set of counters inside a processor that count events such as cycles and stalled slots.
The counters for one workload on one machine turned into throughput, four slot shares and a memory stall share.
The Linux tool that reads the PMU counters around one run of a program.
A program run in place of the arm's real workload because it is expected to load the machine in a similar way.
A small loop built to load one part of a core, such as arithmetic or memory.
A computer that sits beside a robot, outside a data centre.
One chance per cycle for a core to start a piece of work; a core has a fixed number per cycle.
The share of slots that did work that finished.
The share of slots that did work thrown away after a wrong guess.
The share of slots left empty because no instruction was ready.
The share of slots left empty because the executing half of the core could not take more.
The share of cycles the back end spent waiting for data from memory, read from a separate counter.
The bytes per second that can stream from memory to a core.
The time one isolated read from memory takes.
One instruction that computes a x b + c; its rate measures a core's floating-point arithmetic.
A loop that streams through arrays larger than the caches, used to measure memory bandwidth.
A loop where each read gives the address of the next, used to measure memory latency.
The function that sets negative values to zero, applied after a layer of a neural network.
The interface MuJoCo uses for hardware accelerated rendering with no display.
One function launched on the GPU.
NVIDIA's profiler for a single GPU kernel; it reports compute and memory throughput as shares of the GPU's maximum.
The GPU's unit of compute cores.
The GPU units built for the matrix arithmetic of neural networks.
Arm's adjustment that moves the cycles spent recovering from a wrong branch guess from front-end bound to bad speculation.
The imitation-learning policy of section 4 that predicts a chunk of future actions.
A small vision-language-action model, the policy family of section 5.
The latent world model of section 7.
NVIDIA's GPU telemetry tool, which samples activity of the GPU's parts over time.
The Jetson's built-in tool that reports processor, GPU, memory and power readings.
